J U D G M E N T :

1.0 Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the appeal against the order dated 18.04.2016 ("the impugned order" in short) passed by the Ld. Addl. District Magistrate (New Delhi) ("ADM" in short), directing the appellant to pay a penalty of Rs1,00,000/,
under section 53 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short), within 7 days from the date of order.

1 2.0 Facts in brief which are not in dispute, are that : 
 i) on 05.06.2015, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short),
 lifted the sample of "Noodles (Veg. Hakka)", from the  possession of appellant (FBOcumNominee) of M/s  Future Consumer Enterprises Ltd., Shop No. 5&6,
 Hudson Lane, Kingsway Camp, Delhi110 009, where  the said food article was found stored for sale for human  consumption.

One counterpart of the sample under  sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst; 
FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO   ii) The Food Analyst vide his report dated 22.06.2015  opined the sample as misbranded "because there is  violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.3 of the Food Safety  & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation, 2011  ("the said Regulations" in short) as it gives misleading  statement on the label i.e. "No Added MSG".

iii) a copy of the Food Analyst Report was sent to the  appellant on 23.06.2015 giving him an opportunity to  prefer an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst  under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act by sending one part  of the sample to the Referral Lab, if so desired.

But the  appellant did not prefer appeal against the Fo  Analyst's Report; 
 iv) Thereafter, a complaint was filed against t  appellants and others for aforesaid violation before the  Ld. ADM.

On 29.12.2015, the appellants vide   reply while admitting their mistake, submitted that  they have informed the manufacturer not to use the FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO   said packaging any further for packing the noodles.

sentences.text: He passed the impugned order totally ignoring  that the declaration 'No added MSG' printed on the lable  was in substantial compliance of the Regulation 2.2.1.3  of the FSS (P&L) Regulations; and no prejudice was  caused to the consumers;
The appellant/manufacturer had n  added MSG and the declaration only to that effect was  made on the label.
This fact is even apparent from the  Food Analyst's Report, as per which no MSG was found  added to the product.
Thus, such declaration was   deceptive and was not intended to mislead the  consumers.
FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO   4.0 Ld.
Chief Public Prosecutor for the State submitted that as per the appellants' own averment, MSG is even naturally present in certain foods/additives.

Hence, such a declaration of 'No MSG',
without any knowledge/declaration on the appellants' part whether the same is naturally present in the product, could have been deceptive to the consumers.

Such a declaration was therefore,
violative of Regulation 2.2.1.3 of the said Regulations.
Thus, there is no infirmity in the impugned order.

This appeal therefore,

sentences.text: 5.0 I have heard Sh. Kapil Sharma, Advocate for appellant and Sh. Anil, Ld. Chief PP for the State and have perused the record carefully.
6.0 The Ld. ADM has found the appellants guilty  violation of regulation 2.2.1.3 of the said Regulations and has imposed a consolidated penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/ on them.
6.1 The appellants have challenged the impugned order on various grounds.
Before this court, the appellants have contended that the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order being guided by order FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO   of FSSAI dated 31.03.2016.

entities.text: FSAT No 47/16 Ratanjeet Singh Gulati V. FSO   of FSSAI dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pleaded that FSSAI has no power to issue advisories and has placed reliance upon certain judgments in this respect.

Perusal of the impugned order shows that the Ld.
ADM has not referred to any such advisory/order dated 31.03.2016 while passing the order.
6.2 It is also contended by the appellants that the sanction for prosecution was granted without application of mind; and that the Noodles are a proprietary food etc.
These contentions were never raised before the Ld. ADM.
Same is evident from the copy of appellants' Written Statement filed before the Ld. ADM, copy of which has been placed on record by the appellants themselves.
Further, the plea of sanction being not proper was not even pressed during arguments.

6.2.1 It is noteworthy that in the written statement, besides narrating the facts, only the following averments were made by the appellants with respect to the violation of the Regulation 2.2.1.3 of said Regulations :
 "....
 4.

That the statement on the pack of Noodle "No added MSG" w  not to mislead or otherwise in the analysis MSG was not foun  sample of Noodle sent for analysis.

ADM that the packaging has been changed and the declaration 'No added MSG' had been  r e m o v e d . A l t h o u g h , t h e y p r a y e d f o r d i s c h a r g e p l e a d i n g t h a t t h e s a i d l a b e l d i d n o t m i s l e a d , a s M S G w a s not found in the sample food, on analysis.

7.0 Let me refer to Regulation 2.2.1.3 which reads as under :
"2.2 : Labelling 2.2.1: General requirements ....
3 . P r e P a c k a g e d f o o d s h a l l n o t b e d e s c r i b e d o r p r e s e n t e d o n any label or in any labelling manner that is false, misleading or deceptive or is  likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character in any respect." 
7 . 1 F r o m t h e p l a i n r e a d i n g o f t h e a b o v e r e g u l a t i o n , i t i s evident that the food shall not be described on the label in a manner that could mislead/deceive  t h e c o n s u m e r . A d m i t t e d l y , M o n o s o d i u m G l u t a m a t e / M S G , a s a l t o f G l u t a m i c a c i d i s n a t u r a l l y f o u n d i n m a n y c o m m o n f o o d s s u c h a s m i l k , s p i c e s , w h e a t , v e g e t a b l e s e t c .
I t i s a l s o n o t t h e c a s e o f t h e a p p e l l a n t s t h a t t h e y k n e w t h a t t h e M S G w a s n o t n a t u r a l l y p r e s e n t i n t h e s a m p l e f o o d / N o o d l e s ( V e g . H a k k a ) .
Thus, it cannot be disputed that the declaration on the package of sample food that there is no  MSG/'No added MSG' would have misled the consumers had the MSG been naturally  found in the contents of the 'Noodles'/sample food and therefore, the said declaration does contravene Regulation 2.2.1.3. 
7 . 2 I t w o u l d h o w e v e r , b e w o r t h w h i l e t o r e f e r h e r e t o F S S A I ' s o r d e r d a t e d 3 1 . 0 3 . 2 0 1 6 , c o p y o f w h i c h h a s b e e n p l a c e d o n record by Ld. Counsel for the appellants.

sentences.text: ORDER Subject : Clarification on use of Monosodium  Glutamate as flavour enhancer in seasoning for Noodles and Pastas 1 .
U n d e r R e g u l a t i o n 3 .

1 o f t h e F o o d S a f e t y a n d Standards (Food Product Standards and Food Additives), Regulations, 2011, 
Monosodium Glutamate (MSG), a flavour enhancer bearing INS number  6 2 1 , m a y b e a d d e d t o s p e c i f i e d f o o d s a s p e r t h e provisions of Appendix A, subject to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) level and under proper declaration as provided in 2.4.5 (18) of the Food  Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011.
2 . I t i s w i d e l y k n o w n t h a t G l u t a m a t e i s n a t u r a l l y f o u n d in several common foods such as milk, spices, wheat, vegetables, etc.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: MSG is the sodium salt of Glutamic acid and one of the many forms of glutamate.

Presently, there is no analytical method to determine whether MSG was added to the product during its manufacture or was naturally  p r e s e n t i n t h e p r o d u c t . T h i s c a n h o w e v e r b e checked through inspection of the manufacturing premises.
3. To prevent both avoidable harassment/prosecution of Food Business
O p e r a t o r s ( F B O s ) a s w e l l a s t o e n s u r e t h a t

consumers are facilitated to exercise informed choices in respect of what they eat,
 p r o c e e d i n g s m a y b e l a u n c h e d a g a i n s t F B O s o n l y w h e n t h e l a b e l s s t a t e " N o M S G " o r " N o a d d e d M S G " a n d M S G i s actually found in the impugned foodstuff.

Commissioners of Food Safety are advised that specific enforcement/prosecution may not be launched against the manufacturers of Noodles/Pasta on account of presence of  MSG/Glutamic Acid unless it is ascertained by the department that  Monosodium Glutamate flavour enhancer (INS E 621) was deliberately added during the course of manufacture without required declaration on the label as indicated in Para 1 above.
4. This issues with the approval of the Competent Authority.

(Rakesh Chandra Sharma) Director (Enforcement)"
7 . 3 I n v i e w o f t h e f a c t t h a t F S S A I i t s e l f h a s c l a r i f i e d t h a t the proceedings may be initiated only when the labels state "No MSG" or "

No  added MSG" and MSG is actually found in the sample food; and  c o n s i d e r i n g t h e f a c t s a n d c i r c u m s t a n c e s i n t h e instant case i.e., MSG was not found in the sample food/Noodles as per Food Analyst's Report; and also that the corrective steps were immediately  taken and informed to the Ld.ADM, the penalty of Rs.1,00,000/
